blocks.text: 29.11 Delay
blocks.raw_html: 29.11 Delay

blocks.text: Delay includes independent delay lines for each stereo channel, along with a band-pass filter and LFO modulation options.
blocks.raw_html: Delay includes independent delay lines for each stereo channel, along with a band-pass filter and LFO modulation options.

blocks.text: The delay time can be set in tempo-synced beat divisions (Sync) or milliseconds (Time). You can switch between these options using the Delay Time Mode toggles.
blocks.raw_html: The delay time can be set in tempo-synced beat divisions (Sync) or milliseconds (Time). You can switch between these options using the Delay Time Mode toggles.

blocks.text: When set to Sync, you can use the numbered buttons to set the delay time in sixteenth notes. For example, if 4 is selected, the input signal is delayed by four sixteenth notes, which equals one beat (i.e., a quarter note) of delay. Use the Offset sliders to adjust the timing of the sixteenth notes by fractional amounts. Negative values shorten the timing so that the delay occurs slightly earlier than the sixteenth note division, while positive values extend it so that the delay occurs slightly later. You can use Offset to add subtle swing to the delay.

blocks.text: When set to Time, you can delay the input signal anywhere from 1.00 millisecond up to 5.00 seconds.

blocks.text: Activate the Stereo Link toggle to link the delay settings between the left and right channels. Once linked, any adjustments you make to one channel’s delay time are applied to both channels. Offset can be adjusted for each channel independently, even when Stereo Link is enabled.

blocks.text: The Feedback control defines how much of each channel’s output signal is fed back into its delay line input. The feedback loops are independent for each channel, so the signal for the left channel is not fed back into the right channel and vice versa.

blocks.text: You can activate the Freeze button to endlessly cycle the audio in the device’s buffer at the moment the button is pressed. Any new input is ignored until Freeze is deactivated.

blocks.text: The delay signal is preceded by a band-pass filter which can be switched on or off via the Filter toggle. In the display, you can click and drag along the X-axis to adjust the center frequency of the filter, and click and drag along the Y-axis to set the bandwidth. You can also adjust these settings with the Freq and Width sliders.

blocks.text: The delay time and filter frequency can be modulated by an LFO, which makes it possible to achieve a range of sounds from chorus-like effects to chopped glitches.

blocks.text: Use the Rate drop-down menu to choose from the following LFO rate modes: Rate, Time, Synced, Triplet, Dotted, and Sixteenth. The LED next to the LFO Controls toggle flashes in time with the current LFO rate during playback.

blocks.text: Repitch produces a pitch variation when the delay time is changed, which is similar to the behavior of old tape delay units. This mode is enabled by default.

blocks.text: Two additional modes are available via Delay’s context menu or the Show Options menu in the device title bar: Hi-Quality and Dry/Wet - Equal-Loudness.

blocks.text: 29.14 Echo
blocks.raw_html: 29.14 Echo

blocks.text: Echo is a modulation delay effect that lets you set the delay time on two independent delay lines, while giving you control over envelope and filter modulation.

blocks.text: The Channel Mode buttons let you choose between three different modes: Stereo, Ping Pong and Mid/Side.

blocks.text: The Left and Right delay line controls let you choose the delay time, which can be set in beat divisions or milliseconds, depending on the state of the Sync switch. Note that when the Mid/Side channel mode is selected, the Left and Right delay line controls are replaced with Mid and Side knobs.

blocks.text: 29.14.1 Echo Tab

blocks.text: The Echo tab provides a visualization and control of the delay lines and filter parameters.
blocks.raw_html: The Echo tab provides a visualization and control of the delay lines and filter parameters.

blocks.text: The Echo Tunnel’s circular lines represent the individual repeats, progressing from the outside of the tunnel to its center. The distance between the lines indicates the time between the repeats, and the white dots in the middle form a fixed 1/8th note grid for reference. You can adjust the delay times for each delay line by clicking and dragging in the display.

blocks.text: Echo’s Modulation tab contains an LFO that modulates filter frequency and delay time, and an envelope follower that can be blended with the LFO.

blocks.text: You can choose from one of six different modulation waveforms including sine, triangle, sawtooth up, sawtooth down, square, and noise. The selected waveform will appear in the display, which you can drag to adjust the modulation frequency.

blocks.text: Echo’s Character tab contains parameters that control dynamics and add imperfections to your sound.

blocks.text: Gate enables a gate at Echo’s input. It mutes the signal components below its threshold. Threshold sets the threshold level that incoming audio signals must exceed in order to open the gate. Release sets how long it takes for the gate to close after the signal has dropped below the threshold.

blocks.text: 29.19 Filter Delay
blocks.raw_html: 29.19 Filter Delay

blocks.text: The Filter Delay provides three independent delay lines, each preceded by linked low-pass and high-pass filters. This allows applying delay to only certain input signal frequencies, as determined by the filter settings. The feedback from each of the three delays is also routed back through the filters.

blocks.text: Each of the three delays can be switched on and off independently. The Filter Delay device assigns delay 1 to the input signal’s left channel, delay 2 to the left and right channels and delay 3 to the right channel. The Pan controls at the right can override the delay channels’ outputs; otherwise each delay outputs on the channel from which it derives its input.

blocks.text: 29.22 Grain Delay
blocks.raw_html: 29.22 Grain Delay

blocks.text: The Grain Delay effect slices the input signal into tiny particles (called ”grains”) that are then individually delayed and can also have different pitches compared to the original signal source. Randomizing pitch and delay time can create complex masses of sound and rhythm that seem to bear little relationship to the source. This can be very useful in creating new sounds and textures, as well as getting rid of unwelcome house guests, or terrifying small pets (just kidding!).

blocks.text: Hybrid Reverb combines two different approaches to reverberation in one device, blending convolution reverb with a number of digital reverb algorithms. Using multiple routing options and parameters, you can create unique reverb sounds, or use Hybrid Reverb to generate drone-like soundscapes or completely transform any source material.

blocks.raw_html: 29.23.3 Convolution Reverb Engine

blocks.text: A convolution reverb uses recordings of actual spaces (called impulse responses) to create its effect. This allows you to place your sounds in practically any space for which you have a recording. For a more typical reverb sound, this can include some of the most famous halls and studios throughout the world. With a more creative approach, you can use recordings of anything, from snare drums to garbage cans, or even instrumental and vocal recordings!

blocks.raw_html: 29.31 Resonators

blocks.text: The Resonators effect consists of five parallel resonators that add a tonal character to the input signal and can be tuned in semitones or scale degrees. The effect can produce results ranging from plucked-string timbres to vocoder-like tones. It also supports tuning systems.
blocks.raw_html: The Resonators effect consists of five parallel resonators that add a tonal character to the input signal and can be tuned in semitones or scale degrees. The effect can produce results ranging from plucked-string timbres to vocoder-like tones. It also supports tuning systems.

blocks.text: The input signal passes through a filter first, and then into the resonators. Four filter types are available: low-pass, band-pass, high-pass, and notch. You can use the Frequency parameter to adjust the selected filter’s frequency.
blocks.raw_html: The input signal passes through a filter first, and then into the resonators. Four filter types are available: low-pass, band-pass, high-pass, and notch. You can use the Frequency parameter to adjust the selected filter’s frequency.

blocks.text: The device provides two different resonation modes. Mode A provides a more realistic sounding resonation, while Mode B offers an effect that is especially interesting when Resonator I’s Note parameter is set to lower pitches.
blocks.raw_html: The device provides two different resonation modes. Mode A provides a more realistic sounding resonation, while Mode B offers an effect that is especially interesting when Resonator I’s Note parameter is set to lower pitches.

blocks.text: The Decay parameter lets you adjust the amount of time it takes for the resonators to be silent after getting an input signal. The resulting sound will be more sustained and tonal with longer decay times, similar to the behavior of an undamped piano string. As with a real string, the decay time depends on the pitch, so low notes will last longer than higher ones. The Const switch applies a constant decay time regardless of pitch.

blocks.text: You can adjust the brightness of the resulting sound using the Color control.

blocks.text: The first resonator receives both the left and right input channels, while the second and fourth resonators process the left channel, and the third and fifth process the right channel.

blocks.text: The tuning of the resonators depends on whether scale awareness is enabled in the effect or not, or if a tuning system is active. By default, the first resonator defines the root pitch and the other four are tuned relative to this pitch in musical intervals. When scale awareness is enabled, the first resonator is tuned relative to the active clip scale in octave 2 and the remaining resonators are tuned relative to its pitch. When a tuning system is active, the first resonator is tuned to an absolute pitch defined by the tuning, while the remaining resonators are tuned relative to its pitch.

blocks.text: The Note parameter sets the root pitch of all the resonators. By default, the pitch is set in semitones ranging from C-1 to C5. When scale awareness is enabled, the pitch is set in scale degrees. When a tuning system is active, the pitch is set in note indices based on the tuning system’s set of pitches. You can make fine adjustments in cents using the Resonator I Fine Tuning parameter.

blocks.text: All of the resonators have an On/Off toggle and a Gain control. A resonator that is turned off does not consume CPU resources. Turning off the first resonator does not affect the other ones.

blocks.text: Resonators II through V follow the Note parameter defined in Resonator I, but they can each be individually transposed by ±24 semitones or ±21 scale degrees (if the effect is scale aware) using their individual Pitch controls. Additional fine tuning is available through the Resonator II–V Fine Tuning parameters.

blocks.text: The device features the following output controls: Width, Gain, and Dry/Wet. The Width parameter only affects the wet signal and blends the output of Resonators II-V into a mono signal at 0.0%. Gain adjusts the level of the resonated signal unless Dry/Wet is set to 0%. Dry/Wet adjusts the balance between the processed and unprocessed signals.

blocks.text: 29.32 Reverb
blocks.raw_html: 29.32 Reverb

blocks.text: Reverb is an audio effect that simulates the acoustic properties of audio as it echoes throughout a physical space.
blocks.raw_html: Reverb is an audio effect that simulates the acoustic properties of audio as it echoes throughout a physical space.

blocks.text: In the real world, reverberation exists as a product of sound waves that reflect off of rigid surfaces in an environment and the subsequent tonal shaping of these waves by absorbent materials within their trajectory. In a digital context, however, this phenomenon is approximated with a combination of filters and modulated delay lines.
blocks.raw_html: In the real world, reverberation exists as a product of sound waves that reflect off of rigid surfaces in an environment and the subsequent tonal shaping of these waves by absorbent materials within their trajectory. In a digital context, however, this phenomenon is approximated with a combination of filters and modulated delay lines.

blocks.text: The Reverb device provides granular control of all of these factors in order to create unique spaces for audio to travel through that range from intimate recording rooms to massive canyons, and everything in between.

blocks.text: 29.32.1 Input Filter
blocks.raw_html: 29.32.1 Input Filter

blocks.text: The input signal passes first through low and high cut filters, whose X-Y controller allows changing the band’s center frequency (X-axis) and bandwidth (Y-axis). The filters can also be controlled using the sliders located below the X-Y controller. Either filter may be switched off when not needed to save CPU power.

blocks.text: 29.32.2 Early Reflections
blocks.raw_html: 29.32.2 Early Reflections

blocks.text: These are the earliest echoes that you hear after they bounce off a room’s walls, before the onset of the diffused reverberation tail. Their amplitude and distribution give an impression of the room’s character.
blocks.raw_html: These are the earliest echoes that you hear after they bounce off a room’s walls, before the onset of the diffused reverberation tail. Their amplitude and distribution give an impression of the room’s character.

blocks.text: Spin applies modulation to the early reflections. The Amount and Rate sliders control the amount and rate of these modulations respectively. A higher Amount setting tends to provide a less-colored (more spectrally neutral) late diffusion response. If the modulation rate is too high, doppler frequency shifting of the source sound will occur, along with surreal panning effects. Spin may be turned off, using the associated switch, for modest CPU savings.

blocks.text: The Shape control sculpts the prominence of the early reflections, as well as their overlap with the diffused sound. With small values, the reflections decay more gradually and the diffused sound occurs sooner, leading to a larger overlap between these components. With large values, the reflections decay more rapidly and the diffused onset occurs later. A higher value can sometimes improve the source’s intelligibility, while a lower value may give a smoother decay.

blocks.text: 29.32.3 Diffusion Network
blocks.raw_html: 29.32.3 Diffusion Network

blocks.text: The Diffusion Network creates the reverberant tail that follows the early reflections.
blocks.raw_html: The Diffusion Network creates the reverberant tail that follows the early reflections.

blocks.text: High and low shelving filters provide frequency-dependent reverberation decay. The high-frequency decay models the absorption of sound energy due to air, walls and other materials in the room (people, carpeting and so forth). The low shelf provides a thinner decay. Each filter may be turned off to save CPU consumption.

blocks.text: The Diffusion and Scale parameters provide additional control over the diffusion’s density and coarseness, and, when the room size is extremely small, have a large impact on the coloration contributed by the diffusion.

blocks.text: 29.32.4 Chorus
blocks.raw_html: 29.32.4 Chorus

blocks.text: The Chorus section adds a little modulation and motion to the diffusion. You can control the modulation Amount and Rate, or deactivate it altogether.

blocks.text: 29.32.5 Global Settings
blocks.raw_html: 29.32.5 Global Settings

blocks.text: Predelay controls the delay time, in milliseconds, before the onset of the first early reflection. This delays the reverberation relative to the input signal. One’s impression of the size of a real room depends partly on this delay. Typical values for natural sounds range from 1 ms to 25 ms.

blocks.text: The Smooth chooser specifies the behavior of the Size parameter when its value is adjusted. If set to None, the Diffusion Network’s delay times are changed immediately, which can cause artifacts when changing the Size value. If set to Slow or Fast, new delay times are updated over a specific time period, which results in a smoother sound when transitioning between values.

blocks.text: The Size parameter controls the room’s volume. At one extreme, a very large size will lend a shifting, diffused delay effect to the reverb. The other extreme — a very small value — will give it a highly colored, metallic feel.

blocks.text: The Decay control adjusts the time required for this reverb tail to drop to 1/1000th (-60 dB) of its initial amplitude.

blocks.text: The Freeze control freezes the diffuse response of the input sound. When on, the reverberation will sustain almost endlessly. Flat bypasses the high and low shelf filters when Freeze is on. If Flat is off, the frozen reverberation will lose energy in the attenuated frequency bands, depending on the state of the high and low shelving filters. Cut modifies Freeze by preventing the input signal from adding to the frozen reverberation; when off, the input signal will contribute to the diffused amplitude.

At the highest setting of 120 degrees, each ear receives a reverberant channel that is independent of the other (this is also a property of the diffusion in real rooms). The lowest setting mixes the output signal to mono.

owner_requirements.title: Time and tempo-synchronized divisions
owner_requirements.text: Delay has separate left/right delay lines. Sync selects sixteenth-note divisions; selection 4 denotes four sixteenths, one quarter note. Offset shortens timing at negative values and extends it at positive values. Time mode offers 1.00 ms to 5.00 s. These are documented units/range, not sample rounding or tempo-change rules.

owner_requirements.title: Stereo Link and independent offsets
owner_requirements.text: With Stereo Link on, changing one delay time applies to both channels, but each Offset remains independently adjustable. Linking initial unequal values, unlink restoration and simultaneous edits are unresolved.

owner_requirements.title: Feedback paths
owner_requirements.text: Feedback returns each channel output to its own delay input; with Ping Pong off the documented feedback loops do not feed the opposite channel. Feedback gain law, runaway limit and saturation remain U.

owner_requirements.title: Freeze admission and buffer cycling
owner_requirements.text: Freeze endlessly cycles the audio already in the buffer and ignores new input until deactivated. This does not establish a capture length, crossfade, exact periodic output or buffer persistence across save/reset.

owner_requirements.title: Input band-pass filter
owner_requirements.text: The switchable band-pass filter precedes the delay signal. The display X-axis and Freq slider adjust center frequency; Y-axis and Width slider adjust bandwidth. Its transfer function is U.

owner_requirements.title: Modulation targets and section visibility
owner_requirements.text: An LFO modulates delay time and filter frequency through separate Delay and Filter depth sliders. LFO Controls expands the collapsed section; the documented initial display is collapsed. The timing smoothing mode can change the sonic result of modulation. No default values or oscillator phase are established for the pinned build.

owner_requirements.title: LFO modes, shapes and Morph
owner_requirements.text: Rate offers Rate, Time, Synced, Triplet, Dotted and Sixteenth modes. Wave offers Sine, Triangle, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Square, S&H and Wander, with Morph shaping the selected wave. During playback the LED flashes with current LFO rate. Random distributions and phase resets are U.

owner_requirements.title: Timing transitions
owner_requirements.text: Repitch produces a pitch change when delay time changes; Fade crossfades old/new times; Jump changes time immediately and can click during an existing decay. Repitch is the manual-described initial mode, with exact-build defaults U. No smoothing duration or requirement to click is inferred.

owner_requirements.title: Ping Pong
owner_requirements.text: Ping Pong makes the delay signal alternate between left and right channels. Input summing, initial side, stereo normalization and interaction with Link are U.

owner_requirements.title: Dry/Wet
owner_requirements.text: Dry/Wet balances dry and processed audio; 100% is documented for a return so that only processed signal is output. No bit-exact dry bypass, latency or mix equation follows.

owner_requirements.title: Hi-Quality context option
owner_requirements.text: Hi-Quality is available through the device context/Show Options menu. It improves delay interpolation in Repitch/Fade and applies tape-style timing smoothing in Repitch. Numerical interpolation, cost and behavior in Jump are U.

owner_requirements.title: Equal-Loudness context option
owner_requirements.text: Dry/Wet - Equal-Loudness changes between linear and equal-loudness output behavior; enabled 50/50 is described as equally loud for most signals. This qualitative statement is not an equal-power coefficient formula or loudness guarantee for correlated signals.

owner_requirements.title: Channel modes
owner_requirements.text: Echo provides Stereo, Ping Pong and Mid/Side. Mid/Side replaces the Left/Right delay controls with Mid/Side controls. No matrix normalization or sample-level stereo trajectory is specified.

owner_requirements.title: Delay units and Sync Mode
owner_requirements.text: Delay time is in beat divisions with Sync on and milliseconds with Sync off. Notes, Triplet, Dotted and 16th are selectable Sync Modes; changing Sync Mode affects sound only while Sync is on.

owner_requirements.title: Stereo Link and offsets
owner_requirements.text: Stereo Link propagates time, Sync-switch and Sync-Mode edits to both delay lines; Offset remains independent per line. The initial value chosen on linking is U.

owner_requirements.title: Input gain and dry distortion
owner_requirements.text: Input adjusts gain applied to the dry signal; D applies distortion to it. The distortion curve, clipping threshold and gain location beyond this description remain U.

owner_requirements.title: Feedback and inversion
owner_requirements.text: Feedback returns each channel output to delay inputs; Ø inverts output before feeding it back. This documents sign inversion, not a full gain/stability law or parity of the first repeat.

owner_requirements.title: Echo Tunnel
owner_requirements.text: Echo Tunnel displays repeats progressing outside to center; spacing denotes repeat interval, white dots form a fixed eighth-note reference. Dragging the display edits delay times.

owner_requirements.title: Filters and display
owner_requirements.text: Filter enables high-pass and low-pass filtering; each has cutoff and resonance. The triangle shows/hides the Filter Display, whose points also edit filters. Transfer functions, ordering beyond the manual and transition behavior are U.

owner_requirements.title: LFO wave, rate and phase
owner_requirements.text: The Modulation tab offers sine, triangle, saw up, saw down, square and noise. Sync selects beat-based Rate versus Freq in Hz. Display dragging edits frequency; Phase offsets left/right waveforms and 180 degrees denotes opposed phase. Exact wave shapes/noise law are U.

owner_requirements.title: Modulation targets and x4
owner_requirements.text: Mod Delay targets delay time, Modulation x4 multiplies delay-modulation depth by four, and Mod Filter targets the filter. This does not establish a time-domain equation after clipping or smoothing.

owner_requirements.title: Envelope versus LFO source
owner_requirements.text: Env Mix blends the LFO and envelope follower: 0% selects LFO only and 100% envelope only. Envelope detection, attack/release and blending law are U.

owner_requirements.title: Input gate and wet ducking
owner_requirements.text: Gate operates at the input and mutes components below Threshold; Release sets closing time after a drop below threshold. Ducking reduces wet signal while input exceeds its Threshold, with Release after it drops. Equality, detector curve, attenuation amount, sidechain topology and exact timing are U.

owner_requirements.title: Noise and Wobble
owner_requirements.text: Noise adds vintage-character noise with Amount and Morph. Wobble adds irregular delay-time modulation with Amount and Morph. Random processes, seed, spectral law and restart continuity are U.

owner_requirements.title: Repitch versus crossfade
owner_requirements.text: Repitch on produces pitch variation when delay time changes; off crossfades old/new times. No fade duration, resampling kernel or state reset is specified.

owner_requirements.title: Idle shutdown exception
owner_requirements.text: Any application-observable consequence of the documented idle shutdown and Noise+Gate exception remains unknown. No shutdown indicator, CPU criterion, tail cutoff or internal processing mechanism is required; the manual statement is research context only.

owner_requirements.title: Reverb placement and decay
owner_requirements.text: Reverb adjusts added reverberation; Location offers pre delay, post delay and within feedback. Decay lengthens/shortens reverb tail; its kernel and numerical tail are U.

owner_requirements.title: Stereo width, output and mix
owner_requirements.text: Stereo acts on wet width: 0% is mono, above 100% is widened. Output changes processed gain. Dry/Wet balances dry/processed signals and 100% is intended for returns. Equal-Loudness is a Dry/Wet context option; its 50/50 loudness statement applies to most signals and establishes no coefficients.

owner_requirements.title: Three delay inputs and output panning
owner_requirements.text: Three independently enabled delay lines have input selections left, left+right and right respectively. Each output normally uses its source channel; its Pan can override output placement. Input summing/normalization, disabled-line tail and pan law remain U.

owner_requirements.title: Filters and feedback routing
owner_requirements.text: Linked low/high-pass filtering precedes each delay and is also in its feedback path. Each filter has its own switch. X adjusts band frequency and Y bandwidth. A filter bypass is distinct from disabling its entire line.

owner_requirements.title: Sync and fractional timing
owner_requirements.text: Sync expresses time as sixteenth divisions; 4 denotes a quarter note. Percentage adjustment shortens/extends delay fractions in Sync. A displayed number does not define fractional-sample conversion.

owner_requirements.title: Milliseconds editing
owner_requirements.text: Sync off uses milliseconds. Delay Time can be edited by vertical drag or typed value. Accepted numerical range, out-of-range parsing, precision and smoothing remain U.

owner_requirements.title: Feedback
owner_requirements.text: Each Feedback control sets returned output amount. Very high values may produce runaway oscillation; the manual gives no safe maximum, limiter, exact gain or guaranteed finite tail.

owner_requirements.title: Line levels and Dry
owner_requirements.text: Each delay has a volume control offering up to +6 dB. Dry adjusts unprocessed level; minimum is documented for return use. These are independent levels, not a Dry/Wet ratio.

owner_requirements.title: Grains and Frequency
owner_requirements.text: Grain Delay divides input into individually delayed grains that may change pitch. Frequency determines grain size/duration and changes how Pitch and Spray sound. Exact grain schedule/window/overlap and Frequency-to-duration law are U.

owner_requirements.title: X/Y assignments
owner_requirements.text: Parameter rows assign X below the display and Y at its left. Delay Time can be assigned to X; Dry/Wet can be assigned to Y. Pointer mapping and assignment persistence remain U.

owner_requirements.title: Synchronized delay and milliseconds
owner_requirements.text: Sync selects sixteenth divisions with 4 equal to a quarter note and percentage timing adjustment. Sync off selects milliseconds, editable by vertical drag or typing. Randomized grain timing does not establish exact output onset at this nominal delay.

owner_requirements.title: Spray random delay
owner_requirements.text: Spray adds random delay changes; low/high descriptions indicate temporal smearing through disruption of source rhythm. No distribution, maximum offset, seed, replay identity or monotonic audio metric is established.

owner_requirements.title: Pitch and Random Pitch
owner_requirements.text: Pitch transposes grains; Random Pitch varies individual-grain pitches and interacts with Pitch. The pitch-shift method, random distribution, tuning precision and no-op bit identity are U.

owner_requirements.title: Feedback and dry/wet
owner_requirements.text: Feedback returns output to the delay input; high values may run away without a documented bound. Dry/wet balances dry and processed audio and can be assigned to Y. The mix law and random-state behavior in feedback are U.

owner_requirements.title: Input filters
owner_requirements.text: Input first passes through individually switchable low/high cut filters. X controls band center, Y bandwidth; sliders offer the same controls. Cutoff laws, slope and bypass transition are U.

owner_requirements.title: Early reflections and Spin
owner_requirements.text: Early reflections precede the diffuse tail. Spin modulates early reflections with Amount and Rate and can be disabled. Large rates may cause Doppler shifts/panning; no trajectory or threshold is specified.

owner_requirements.title: Shape
owner_requirements.text: At smaller Shape values early reflections decay more gradually and diffuse onset is sooner, increasing overlap. Larger values yield quicker reflection decay and later diffuse onset. No continuous mapping or exact onset/decay metric follows.

owner_requirements.title: Diffuse tail and shelving
owner_requirements.text: The Diffusion Network generates the tail. Independent high/low shelving filters shape frequency-dependent decay and can be turned off. Filter transfer, decay multipliers and frequency equality are U.

owner_requirements.title: Diffusion and Scale
owner_requirements.text: Diffusion and Scale control tail density/coarseness, with pronounced coloration at extremely small room Size. No delay-line topology or parameter law is established.

owner_requirements.title: Chorus
owner_requirements.text: Chorus modulates the diffusion with Amount and Rate and has an independent disable switch. Exact oscillator phases, waves and reset state are U.

owner_requirements.title: Predelay
owner_requirements.text: Predelay is in milliseconds before the first early reflection. The manual describes 1-25 ms as typical natural-room choices; this is not its allowed range or rounding rule.

owner_requirements.title: Size and Smooth
owner_requirements.text: Size controls virtual room volume. Smooth None changes diffusion delay times immediately; Slow/Fast update them over a period. Exact periods, interpolation and transition ordering are U.

owner_requirements.title: Decay definition
owner_requirements.text: Decay denotes time for tail amplitude to fall to 1/1000 of its initial amplitude (-60 dB). This defines the documented quantity, not a calibrated output crossing in a multiband/modulated signal, finite tail termination or a numerical exponential.

owner_requirements.title: Freeze, Flat and Cut
owner_requirements.text: Freeze sustains the diffuse response almost endlessly. With Freeze on, Flat bypasses high/low shelves; Flat off permits energy loss in attenuated bands according to shelf state. Cut prevents new input contributing to frozen reverberation; Cut off admits it. No exact infinite tail or bypass law outside Freeze follows.

owner_requirements.title: Stereo, Density and output
owner_requirements.text: Stereo lowest setting mixes output to mono; 120 degrees describes independent reverberant channels. Density trades quality/performance, with Sparse and High named endpoints. Reflect and Diffuse independently scale their components; Dry/Wet balances overall dry/wet. No coefficient matrix, CPU count or mix law is specified.

owner_requirements.title: Wet send and predelay
owner_requirements.text: Send changes gain feeding reverb while leaving dry signal unaffected. Predelay offers time/beat-synced units; each mode has an independent Feedback setting. These are distinct from the algorithm additional Delay. Timing units, feedback persistence across mode toggles and sample conversion need separate evidence.

owner_requirements.title: Serial routing
owner_requirements.text: Serial sends convolution output into the algorithm engine. The convolution stays active; Blend 100/0 gives convolution-only output, while 0/100 gives algorithmic output fed by convolution. It is not raw-input algorithm-only at the second endpoint. The interpolation law is U.

owner_requirements.title: Parallel routing
owner_requirements.text: Parallel keeps convolution and algorithm engines separate. Blend 100/0 gives pure convolution and 0/100 pure algorithmic output. Exact summation/gain law is U.

owner_requirements.title: Single-engine routing and disabled controls
owner_requirements.text: Algorithm uses only the algorithm engine; Convolution only convolution. Unused-engine controls are grayed out. Blend has no effect in either single-engine route. Stored hidden values, CPU behavior and sample-identical no-op output are U.

owner_requirements.title: IR selection and display
owner_requirements.text: Category and IR selectors choose impulses; arrows advance continuously across category boundaries. Waveform reflects Attack/Decay/Size changes. Ten documented categories are Early Reflections, Real Places, Chambers and Large Rooms, Made for Drums, Halls, Plates, Springs, Bigger Spaces, Textures and User. Exact installed IR list/version is U.

owner_requirements.title: User IR import and removal
owner_requirements.text: Dropping an audio file on the waveform adds it as an IR; audio siblings in its folder are also added. Remove the device and add it again: previously added User samples no longer appear in User until added again. This does not define saved-Set restoration, supported codec set, recursion, file sorting or cleanup of source bytes.

owner_requirements.title: Convolution envelope
owner_requirements.text: Attack/Decay control the IR amplitude envelope attack/decay times; Size controls relative IR size. Exact envelope, resampling, normalization, latency and stereo-channel convolution are U.

owner_requirements.title: Algorithms and common controls
owner_requirements.text: Algorithms are Dark Hall, Quartz, Shimmer, Tides and Prism, with controls changing by selection. All have Decay, Size, Delay and Freeze. Decay denotes approximate time to -60 dB, Size virtual room size and Delay an additional algorithmic predelay in milliseconds. No exact kernel, sample delay or tolerance is established.

owner_requirements.title: Freeze versus Freeze In
owner_requirements.text: Freeze blocks input to the algorithmic engine and sets decay to infinite for sustained output. Freeze In adds new input to frozen reverberation. This contract is algorithmic; it does not establish freezing convolution output, state persistence or numerical infinite duration.

owner_requirements.title: Dark Hall controls
owner_requirements.text: Dark Hall provides Damping for high-frequency filtering, Mod for tail movement, Shape from small/resonant toward large/diffused, Bass X low-tail crossover and Bass Mult low-tail decay scaling. Long decay with tiny Size can give gong-like resonance; no guaranteed timbre or crossover law follows.

owner_requirements.title: Quartz controls
owner_requirements.text: Quartz provides Damping (high filtering), Lo Damp (low filtering), Mod (tail movement), Diffusion (sparse to dense) and Distance (closer/denser to farther/more-spaced reflections). No monotonic waveform statistic or exact reflection schedule is specified.

owner_requirements.title: Shimmer controls and zero amount
owner_requirements.text: Shimmer includes Damping, Mod, Diffusion, Pitch in semitones and Shimmer amount. Pitch-shifted feedback creates rising/falling tails; Shimmer=0% applies no pitch shifting and increasing amount makes pitched signal more present. Size affects spacing of echoes on percussive material. No resampling, diffusion threshold kernel or feedback stability law is specified.

owner_requirements.title: Tides modulation
owner_requirements.text: Tides modulates output spectrum with a multiband filter. Damping controls high filtering; Tide controls texture intensity; Wave morphs noise (0%) to sine (50%) to square (100%); Phase=180 degrees opposes left/right modulation; Rate uses beat divisions with Triplet/16th/Dotted variations. Random spectra and phase/timing precision are U.

owner_requirements.title: Prism band decay controls
owner_requirements.text: Prism is described as based on spectrally flat velvet noise. Low Mult and High Mult scale respective tail-band decays; X over sets the band boundary. Noise process, crossover filters, gain normalization and exact decay curves are U.

owner_requirements.title: EQ placement and enable
owner_requirements.text: EQ has its own tab and toggle. The documented usual position follows both engines; Pre Algo places it before the algorithm engine regardless of selected reverb routing. This text does not resolve every Convolution-only inactive-algorithm topology or changing-tail transition.

owner_requirements.title: EQ bands
owner_requirements.text: Four EQ bands include low/high bands switchable between pass filters and shelves, with 6 to 96 dB/octave slope range in pass modes; two middle peak bands cover the frequency range. Exact band domains, slope menu steps, cutoff/Q and digital transfer functions are U.

owner_requirements.title: Wet width and Dry/Wet
owner_requirements.text: Stereo controls wet width with mono at 0% and widening above 100%; Dry/Wet balances processed/dry audio and 100% is documented for return use. No mono matrix, pan gain or mixing formula is established.

owner_requirements.title: Vintage
owner_requirements.text: Vintage increasingly emulates lower sample rates/bit depths, with four presets Subtle, Old, Older and Extreme. No actual sample rates, bit depths, noise shaping or exact distortion is established.

owner_requirements.title: Bass Mono
owner_requirements.text: Bass Mono converts frequencies below 180 Hz of the described output signal to mono. The source does not settle dry-path participation, crossover transition/filter slopes, equality at 180 Hz or channel summation coefficients.

owner_requirements.title: Five resonators and mode
owner_requirements.text: Five parallel resonators add tonal character. Mode A and B select distinct resonance modes; descriptions of realistic/low-pitched effects establish no modal kernel or numerical equivalence.

owner_requirements.title: Input filter
owner_requirements.text: Input filtering precedes resonators, with low-pass, band-pass, high-pass and notch types, and Frequency controlling selected filter frequency. Filter order, slope and switching tails are U.

owner_requirements.title: Decay, Const and Color
owner_requirements.text: Decay changes resonator sustain; normal pitch-dependent decay lasts longer at lower notes. Const selects pitch-independent decay; Color controls brightness. Exact time definition, frequency law, equality and spectrum are U.

owner_requirements.title: Channel assignments
owner_requirements.text: Resonator I receives left+right, II/IV left only, III/V right only. Summation scaling and the output stereo matrix are U.

owner_requirements.title: Root tuning and context
owner_requirements.text: Without scale awareness/tuning, I sets root and others follow musical intervals. With scale awareness, I is relative to active clip scale in octave 2; others relative to I. With tuning active, I uses an absolute tuning-defined pitch and others relative to it. Exact tuning precedence, no-active-clip fallback and changes during a tail remain U.

owner_requirements.title: Note, Fine and relative ranges
owner_requirements.text: Default Note is semitones C-1 to C5; scale awareness changes to scale degrees, tuning to note indices. Fine I edits cents. II-V transpose relative to I by ±24 semitones or ±21 scale degrees and have individual Fine controls. Note-label ranges do not establish internal numbering, quantization or frequency calculation.

owner_requirements.title: Independent enable and gain
owner_requirements.text: Every resonator has On/Off and Gain. Turning I off leaves others active; a disabled resonator is described as consuming no CPU, but this is not an application CPU benchmark or silence/tail oracle.

owner_requirements.title: Wet width, gain and balance
owner_requirements.text: Width acts only on wet output and at 0% blends II-V to mono. Gain adjusts resonated level unless Dry/Wet=0%. Dry/Wet balances paths. No claim is made that I stereo mapping is determined by the II-V statement.

assessments.quote: 29.11 Delay
assessments.assessment: Exact source heading/ancestry only; no input/action/output or completion credit.

assessments.quote: Delay includes independent delay lines for each stereo channel, along with a band-pass filter and LFO modulation options.
assessments.assessment: Independent stereo-line role represented by001/003/009; feedback/channel law is not a kernel.

assessments.quote: The delay time can be set in tempo-synced beat divisions (Sync) or milliseconds (Time). You can switch between these options using the Delay Time Mode toggles.
assessments.assessment: 001actually selects Sync and Time; named toggles/units represented, no tempo-event schedule.

assessments.quote: When set to Sync, you can use the numbered buttons to set the delay time in sixteenth notes. For example, if 4 is selected, the input signal is delayed by four sixteenth notes, which equals one beat (i.e., a quarter note) of delay. Use the Offset sliders to adjust the timing of the sixteenth notes by fractional amounts. Negative values shorten the timing so that the delay occurs slightly earlier than the sixteenth note division, while positive values extend it so that the delay occurs slightly later. You can use Offset to add subtle swing to the delay.
assessments.assessment: 001selects4 and inspects Offset; negative/positive role represented, not measured swing/sample delay.

assessments.quote: When set to Time, you can delay the input signal anywhere from 1.00 millisecond up to 5.00 seconds.
assessments.assessment: 001actually enters both documented Time endpoints; accepted-target/sample rounding remains U.

assessments.quote: Activate the Stereo Link toggle to link the delay settings between the left and right channels. Once linked, any adjustments you make to one channel’s delay time are applied to both channels. Offset can be adjusted for each channel independently, even when Stereo Link is enabled.
assessments.assessment: 002actually links then edits LEFT time and RIGHT Offset. Reverse-side time propagation and LEFT Offset remain unexercised direction branches (G01), initial-link winner U.

assessments.quote: The Feedback control defines how much of each channel’s output signal is fed back into its delay line input. The feedback loops are independent for each channel, so the signal for the left channel is not fed back into the right channel and vice versa.
assessments.assessment: 003uses LEFT pulse with0/40feedback and productive repeat. RIGHT-input mirror needs its own positive before cross-channel absence (G02); no new gain/stability law.

assessments.quote: You can activate the Freeze button to endlessly cycle the audio in the device’s buffer at the moment the button is pressed. Any new input is ignored until Freeze is deactivated.
assessments.assessment: 004actually admits A/B with Freeze-off control, establishes frozen nonzero A then applies B, releases on freshrun. True admission subset; bufferlength/capture/tail persistence U, not anotherdeviceFreeze.

assessments.quote: The delay signal is preceded by a band-pass filter which can be switched on or off via the Filter toggle. In the display, you can click and drag along the X-axis to adjust the center frequency of the filter, and click and drag along the Y-axis to set the bandwidth. You can also adjust these settings with the Freq and Width sliders.
assessments.assessment: 005actually operates X/Y and Freq/Width plus Filter switch under wet F2; genuine effect-positive retained, filter law U.

assessments.quote: The delay time and filter frequency can be modulated by an LFO, which makes it possible to achieve a range of sounds from chorus-like effects to chopped glitches.
assessments.assessment: 006actually activates each depth separately; no silent modulator baseline. Rate/Wave selections versus enumeration and three smoothing-context combinations remain bounded inputs (G03/G04).

assessments.quote: By default, the full LFO section is collapsed and only the delay time and filter modulation controls are shown below the band-pass display. You can use the LFO Controls toggle to expand the LFO section and access additional modulation options.
assessments.assessment: 006actually expands/collapses LFO. Manualcollapsed default context not exact-build constructor law.

assessments.quote: The Delay slider sets the amount of LFO modulation that is applied to the delay time, while the Filter slider sets the modulation amount for the filter frequency.
assessments.assessment: 006actual separate Delay/Filter edits retained; productive destination contribution must precede later effect/noeffect, not flags.

assessments.quote: Use the Rate drop-down menu to choose from the following LFO rate modes: Rate, Time, Synced, Triplet, Dotted, and Sixteenth. The LED next to the LFO Controls toggle flashes in time with the current LFO rate during playback.
assessments.assessment: 007enumerates all6Rate modes and observes LED during transport, not actual selecting/editing each mode (G03). No LEDclock/timing tolerance.
